4: ![title-img](https://nsm09.casimages.com/img/2025/05/31//2505310207423242518595349.png)
5: 
6: The `ftxui::component` module defines the logic that produces interactive
7: components that respond to user events (keyboard, mouse, etc.).
8: 
9: The @subpage module-component-examples section provides a collection of examples.
10: 
11: A `ftxui::App` defines a main loop that renders a component.
12: 
13: A `ftxui::Component` is a shared pointer to a `ftxui::ComponentBase`. The latter defines:
14:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::Render()`: How to render the interface.
15:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::OnEvent()`: How to react to events.
16:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::Add()`: Construct a parent/child relationship
17:     between two components. The tree of components is used to define how to
18:     navigate using the keyboard.
19: 
20: `ftxui::Element` are used to render a single frame.
21: 
22: `ftxui::Component` are used to render dynamic user interface, producing multiple
23: frame, and updating its state on events.
24: 
25: [Gallery](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples_2component_2gallery_8cpp-example.html) of multiple components. ([demo](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples/?file=component/gallery))
26: 
27: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/147247330-b60beb9f-e665-48b4-81c0-4b01ee95bc66.png)

46: ## Filtered input
47: 
48: One can filter out the characters received by the input component, using
49: `ftxui::CatchEvent`.
50: 
51: ```cpp
52: std::string phone_number;
53: Component input = Input(&phone_number, "phone number");
54: 
55: // Filter out non-digit characters.
56: input |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
57:   return event.is_character() && !std::isdigit(event.character()[0]);
58: });
59: 
60: // Filter out characters past the 10th one.
61: input |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
62:   return event.is_character() && phone_number.size() >= 10;
63: });
64: ```

135: # Slider {#component-slider}
136: 
137: Represents a slider object that consists of a range with binned intermediate
138: intervals. It can be created by `ftxui::Slider()`.

146: # Renderer {#component-renderer}
147: 
148: Produced by: `ftxui::Renderer()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp. This
149: component decorate another one by using a different function to render an
150: interface.
151: 
152: Example:
153: ```cpp
154: auto inner = [...]
155: 
156: auto renderer = Renderer(inner, [&] {
157:   return inner->Render() | border
158: });
159: ```
160: 
161: `ftxui::Renderer` also supports the component decorator pattern:
162: ```cpp
163: auto component = [...]
164: component = component
165:   | Renderer([](Element e) { return e | border))
166:   | Renderer(bold)
167: ```
168: 
169: As a short hand, you can also compose a component with an element decorator:
170: ```cpp
171: auto component = [...]
172: component = component | border | bold;
173: ```
174: 
175: # CatchEvent {#component-catchevent}
176: 
177: Produced by: `ftxui::CatchEvent()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp.
178: This component decorate others, catching events before the underlying component.
179: 
180: Examples:
181: ```cpp
182: auto screen = App::TerminalOutput();
183: auto renderer = Renderer([] {
184:   return text("My interface");
185: });
186: auto component = CatchEvent(renderer, [&](Event event) {
187:   if (event == Event::Character('q')) {
188:     screen.ExitLoopClosure()();
189:     return true;
190:   }
191:   return false;
192: });
193: screen.Loop(component);
194: ```
195: 
196: The `ftxui::CatchEvent` can also be used as a decorator:
197: ```cpp
198: component = component
199:   | CatchEvent(handler_1)
200:   | CatchEvent(handler_2)
201:   | CatchEvent(handler_3)
202:   ;
203: ```
204: 
205: # Collapsible {#component-collapsible}
206: 
207: Useful for visual elements whose visibility can be toggled on or off by the
208: user. Essentially, this is the combination of the `ftxui::Checkbox()` and
209: `ftxui::Maybe()` components.
210: 
211: ```cpp
212: auto collapsible = Collapsible("Show more", inner_element);
213: ```
214: 
215: # Maybe {#component-maybe}
216: 
217: Produced by: `ftxui::Maybe()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp.
218: This component can be utilized to show/hide any other component via a boolean or
219: a predicate.
220: 
221: Example with a boolean:
222: ```cpp
223: bool show = true;
224: auto component = Renderer([]{ return "Hello World!"; });
225: auto maybe_component = Maybe(component, &show)
226: ```
227: 
228: Example with a predicate:
229: ```cpp
230: auto component = Renderer([]{ return "Hello World!"; });
231: auto maybe_component = Maybe(component, [&] { return time > 10; })
232: ```
233: 
234: As usual, `ftxui::Maybe` can also be used as a decorator:
235: ```cpp
236: component = component
237:   | Maybe(&a_boolean)
238:   | Maybe([&] { return time > 10; })
239:   ;
240: ```

248: and handles keyboard/mouse navigation.

251:

257: 
258: Produced by: `ftxui::Container::Tab()` from
259: "ftxui/component/component.hpp". It takes a list of components and displays
260: only one of them. This is useful for implementing a tab bar.
